Your brand's reputation now lives inside a new algorithm: one that's based on AI searches made in tools like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini. One hallucinated fact, one competitor-favoring answer, and the trust, traffic, and sales can vanish overnight. And with ChatGPT usage soaring and Google's AI answers appearing in nearly half of all searches even on a traditional search engine, the risk (and opportunity) has never been bigger. Generative engine optimization (GEO) is the next generation of SEO, and using LLM visibility tools is essential for understanding how your brand shows up. These tools track where and how your brand appears in AI responses, flag negative sentiment, and spot when competitors start stealing your spotlight. I've researched nearly 50 LLM monitoring tools—and tested as many as I could get my hands on—to deliver the definitive shortlist of proven performers. Beyond surface-level features, I'll dig into each tool's ideal applications so you can pick the one that will help amplify your brand's presence in the AI ecosystem. How we evaluate and test apps Our best apps roundups are written by humans who've spent much of their careers using, testing, and writing about software. Unless explicitly stated, we spend dozens of hours researching and testing apps, using each app as it's intended to be used and evaluating it against the criteria we set for the category. We're never paid for placement in our articles from any app or for links to any site—we value the trust readers put in us to offer authentic evaluations of the categories and apps we review. For more details on our process, read the full rundown of how we select apps to feature on the Zapier blog . When I evaluated these LLM monitoring tools, I didn't just skim product pages. I interacted with them as a user and SEO/GEO expert with skin in the game, creating accounts, watching demo videos, booking product walkthroughs, and reading the product documentation. Then, when I was able to get hands-on access, I put each AI search optimization tool through scenarios such as those you'd expect to face as a user: monitoring specific brand mentions, discovering which prompts are driving traffic, and brainstorming what new keywords or prompts a brand might want to be associated with. I tested how they handle different AI search engines, dug into reporting capabilities, and also tested the account setup process. After all that digging, here are the factors I found to be the most important for choosing the best LLM monitoring tool. Just remember: this is such a new software category that no app checks every single box quite yet. Tracking visibility across all AI engines : LLM outputs vary by platform, so you need visibility into how your brand appears across multiple popular generative engines. This ensures you're not blindsided by gaps in one platform, especially those where your customers hang out most. Providing insights and action items : Great LLM visibility tools do more than passively monitor—they interpret what's happening and suggest clear, actionable steps to improve brand positioning. Pay extra attention to platforms that proactively share useful research and best practices. Uncovering trends and patterns : Tracking changes over time helps you spot patterns, whether your brand's visibility is rising, slipping, or reacting to competitor moves—enabling you to respond proactively. Prioritize tools that offer at-a-glance trend oversight. Exploring conversation data (not just the outputs) : Understanding the full context of how users interact with AI engines—including follow-up questions, conversation flow, and the nuanced ways your brand appears throughout multi-turn exchanges—provides deeper insights than simply tracking final outputs. This helps you identify opportunities to appear in related queries and understand the customer journey within AI conversations. Citation source detection : When LLMs cite sources, you want to know which ones. This helps identify high-performing internal pages, potential misinformation sources, and partnership opportunities. Brand visibility scoring (also known as share of voice) : Quantifying how your brand shows up in AI outputs compared to competitors and changes over time helps to measure progress and set concrete goals. Brand sentiment analysis : It's not just about whether you're mentioned, but how . Sentiment analysis helps you track the emotional tone of AI mentions so you can take steps to safeguard brand perception. Competitor benchmarking : Benchmarking against competitors shows whether you're leading, lagging, or keeping pace. AI crawler visibility/technical analysis : This helps you determine if your pages are structured and accessible for AI-driven indexing (and gives you something tangible to focus on if they aren't). Keep in mind that best practices are still being established and constantly changing, but it's good to start somewhere. Integration features : I handed out bonus points for the LLM visibility tools that play nicely with workflow tools like Zapier for seamless automation. It's also worth noting that some tools (like ZipTie) track LLM responses using methods that mimic real user behavior rather than relying solely on APIs. This approach can produce more accurate results since it better reflects what actual users see. There's just a little caveat: LLMs are non-deterministic by nature, meaning the same prompt on the same answer engine at the same time can still produce variations in responses. It's more art than science at this point, so you should expect some fluctuation in the results. Lastly, when choosing a platform, you should factor in your available budget and the value of the offering. In addition to the features mentioned previously, you'll also want to determine the cost per prompt, how it grows in terms of how often you run it, how many AI search engines you're tracking, and the specific geographical regions you're targeting. Clearscope pricing: From $129/month for the Essentials plan Best AI visibility platform for local tracking Yext Scout Image source: Yext Scout Yext Scout pros: AI visibility by individual brand location Agents that improve your location-based visibility for you Connects to a broader suite of brand visibility tools Yext Scout cons: Works best alongside the rest of the Yext platform Designed for enterprises, making it too powerful for small and midmarket businesses A lot of AI visibility trackers tell you how your brand shows up nationally. But that scope becomes an issue when your company has multiple locations, and you want to know how each one appears in AI. Yext's Scout tool breaks down AI brand monitoring by location. My favorite Yext Scout feature is its map showing how much visibility each of your locations has in high-intent searches based on engine data from the big players, like ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and Perplexity. Hexagons in various colors show your visibility in the corresponding location, so you can know how each of your branches is doing at a glance. Based on this location data, Yext Scout also recommends actions that you can send agents to perform across Yext's marketing tools . These agents do require you to use the rest of the Yext platform, which could be a negative if you're just looking for an AI visibility tool. But if you're willing to go all in on Yext, Scout offers similarly powerful features to other tools on this list. It measures performance against your 20 closest competitors per scan, based on location and trends, so you know which nearby businesses are showing up in AI. Sentiment analysis brings up recurring themes in AI outputs related to your brand, and citation tracking shows which sources those answers use to pinpoint what content to change. As with the rest of the Yext platform, Yext Scout has a very specific user in mind—enterprises with hundreds to thousands of locations. So if you run a handful of sites, your business might be a little too local to get the most out of Yext Scout. Yext Scout pricing: By request; third-party pricing info suggests at least $199/month Which LLM monitoring tool should you choose? Unfortunately, to get everything you want out of an AI visibility tool right now, you may need to use (and pay for) more than one. But even if you're willing to pay top dollar, measuring LLM visibility is still a bit of a black box. In a sense, we're trying to find a way to work around and measure data that the LLMs are currently locking up. Plus, there are new AI visibility tools popping up left and right as GEO grows as a specialty. A few tools I tested that hit on a lot of the important features and almost made the list include: Goodie , Amplitude , AthenaHQ , Am I on AI? , Rankshift , XFunnel , Knowatoa , Waikay , Evertune , Superlines , RankScale , Scrunch , and SISTRIX . Yes, it's a little messy and definitely imperfect, but waiting for perfect data means missing the opportunity to shape how AI platforms talk about your brand right now—and that's a risk no forward-thinking marketer can afford to take. text: AI visibility platforms, also called LLM tracking tools, measure how a brand appears in generated answers: mentions, citations, answer placement, sentiment, competitors, and how those signals change over time. The 18 platforms below differ in their monitored engines, prompt sampling, evidence, limits, and what happens after a gap is reported. Answer engine optimization (AEO) tools and generative engine optimization (GEO) tools are buyer categories within AI visibility software. Software sold under either label measures the same kind of answer-level evidence, so this guide evaluates both categories with one rubric and one table. For the concepts and workflows behind each label, see what answer engine optimization is and what generative engine optimization is . [!TIP] Looking for enterprise AI visibility tracking? If your goal is to immediately monitor and benchmark your brand's citations across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude, and Google AI Overviews, explore the dedicated Search Atlas LLM Visibility Platform . This comparative guide evaluates 18 standalone software options across the broader market. Results are directional. AI answers vary with prompt wording, location, account context, model updates, retrieval conditions, and run timing. A platform's result is a sample, not a permanent ranking. Search Atlas publishes this comparison and sells LLM Visibility, so Search Atlas appears first and is evaluated by the same fields as every other platform. The most useful comparison is controlled: use your own buyer questions, hold the prompt set steady, ask what each plan includes, and inspect a sample of responses yourself. Key takeaways AI visibility platforms, including software sold as AEO or GEO tools, report different answer-level signals: mentions, citations, first-mention position, sentiment, and share of voice. Engine lists are not interchangeable. A vendor may list a model, an answer interface, a crawler, or an indexed prompt dataset. Prompt origin matters. A platform may use your prompts, vendor-generated prompts, keyword-derived prompts, or a real-user panel. Some platforms report gaps; others recommend work, draft content, publish through a CMS, or change what AI agents receive from a site. Export and API access ranges from PDF and CSV reports to REST APIs and MCP connections, so confirm the channel before relying on a platform for internal reporting. Public price, billing term, trial language, usage limits, add-ons, and unavailable fields belong in separate columns. No platform is the universal winner. The right fit depends on engines, sampling, evidence, governance, budget, and desired workflow. TL;DR What are the best AI visibility tools? The best fit depends on the job. Search Atlas fits teams that want AI visibility tracking alongside SEO, content, and execution. Profound, Conductor, and Athena fit broader enterprise workflows. Peec, Otterly, Waikay, and Geneo pair monitoring with recommendations, while SE Visible, Trackerly, and LLMrefs focus on reporting. Mangools offers a free first check. Ahrefs Brand Radar fits teams already using Ahrefs for research. Scrunch changes what verified AI agents receive from a site, while Evertune adds a large prompt panel, advertising, and content activation. Are AEO tools and GEO tools different products? AEO tools and GEO tools are buyer labels for the same category of AI visibility software. Both categories can be compared on the same fields: prompts, engines, citations, competitors, sentiment, history, alerts, exports, and reporting. How should I compare AI visibility platforms? Compare the same prompt set, engine coverage, run cadence, citation detail, competitor scope, export/API access, plan limits, price term, and path from finding a gap to acting on it. Can one week prove that a platform improves visibility? No. One week can test data collection, prompt fit, evidence quality, and workflow usability. It cannot establish that a platform caused a later visibility change. What AEO and GEO tools measure AEO and GEO tools measure brand presence inside AI-generated answers and the evidence behind each result, rather than page position in a conventional search results page. A useful platform reports each of these fields separately: Prompt coverage: the buyer questions that run, who wrote them, and how many the plan allows. Engine and model coverage: the answer interfaces and models sampled on the plan you would buy. Citations and source URLs: cited domains and pages behind each answer, where the vendor exposes them. Competitor visibility: how named competitors appear for the same prompts, often reported as share of voice. Sentiment or framing: the tone and description an answer attaches to the brand. History: change across runs over time, plus how long results are retained. Alerts: notifications when a tracked signal changes, which are different from scheduled reports. The table records where each vendor states alerts, how they are delivered, and where alerts are user-built rather than native. Exports: CSV, XLSX, Google Sheets, Looker Studio, API, or MCP access to prompt-level data. Reporting: dashboards, scheduled or white-label reports, and shareable views for stakeholders. A mention names the brand. A citation links or attributes an answer to a source. Sentiment describes the tone associated with the brand. Share of voice compares a brand's presence with competitors within a defined prompt set; learn the mathematical weighting in our guide to AI share of voice . These signals answer different questions and should not be collapsed into one number without understanding the calculation. Engine and citation coverage are different Read engine lists literally. ChatGPT, ChatGPT Search, ChatGPT with browsing, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, Gemini, and a crawler are different measurement surfaces. A vendor can monitor an answer interface, an underlying model, an indexed prompt corpus, or a site's AI-bot traffic without measuring the same thing as another vendor. Plan-level coverage matters as much as the headline list. Ask for the exact engine list for the plan you would buy, prompt limits, refresh cadence, and paid add-ons. Citation reporting also has several meanings. A platform may show the URL cited in a response, group sources by type, identify domains that influence answers, analyze native-search citations, or show source pages in a separate research index. These fields are not one universal citation metric. Prompt datasets need the same care. A vendor-generated prompt, keyword-derived prompt, buyer-entered prompt, and real-user panel answer different measurement questions. A real-user panel can add demand context, but it does not make every resulting answer a direct observation of an individual user's session. Pricing, limits, and evidence quality Compare the price with the unit behind it. A monthly fee may buy prompts, credits, checks, model runs, workspaces, or a mixture. A credit may represent one prompt on one platform for one refresh, while another vendor may price a prompt group or recurring plan. Ask vendors to calculate the cost of your actual prompt set. Billing terms must stay attached to every price. Scrunch Starter is $250 per month billed annually or $300 month-to-month. Rankscale Essentials is $17 per month on yearly billing. Writesonic Starter is $79 per month billed annually. SE Visible's annual dollar figure is unavailable, even though an annual discount is stated. Athena's annual percentage discount is stated, but its annual dollar amount is unavailable. Trial language varies. Conductor states three weeks with no card. Profound states 50 prompts daily for seven days. Scrunch states seven days with no card. SE Visible states 10 days. Trackerly states seven days on every plan. Otterly's pages conflict on seven versus 14 days, so this guide says only “free trial.” HubSpot AEO's trial wording also conflicts, so its duration is not presented as settled. When vendor pages conflict, the table states the conflict. When a vendor does not state a field, the field is unavailable. No field is filled from a competitor review or inferred from a similar product. Buyer checklist Required engines: Which engines and answer interfaces must the plan cover? Are they included or add-ons? Prompt set: Can you add, edit, group, pause, and reuse buyer questions? Prompt origin: Are prompts vendor-generated, keyword-derived, user-defined, or panel-based? Sampling cadence: How often does each prompt run, and how many runs support a reported value? Location and context: Can the platform control country, language, device, account, or other context? Citation detail: Does it show cited URLs, source domains, source type, citation position, or only a count? Competitor scope: Can you compare the same prompts and intent across named competitors? Trend data: How far back does history go? Is raw-response retention stated? Exports and API: Can the team export raw prompt-level data or connect an internal report? Governance: Are approvals, roles, audit history, and CMS permissions clear? Actionability: Does the platform report, recommend, draft, publish, or change an AI-facing experience? Budget: What does the plan meter, and what does the complete prompt set cost at the intended cadence? See our LLM visibility tracking plan for a repeatable measurement design and AI search visibility reporting for agencies for agency workflows. Search Atlas disclosure and fit Search Atlas publishes this guide and sells LLM Visibility. Search Atlas is listed first, receives no numeric score, and is not presented as the best overall platform. Search Atlas LLM Visibility measures mentions, citations, sentiment, share of voice, and competitor visibility across topics and prompts. Answer Engine Insights connects visibility findings to Content Genius and OTTO, while citation data can support Digital PR and authority workflows. Search Atlas fits teams that want measurement connected to a broader SEO and execution platform. Teams that want reporting only may prefer a specialist platform with a narrower scope. Teams that need a particular engine, export, cadence, or governance control should verify that field on the plan they would purchase. See AI Visibility for the first-check experience and LLM Visibility for the ongoing workflow. One-week comparison method A one-week trial can test whether a platform's data is understandable, repeatable, and useful. It cannot prove that a platform caused an improvement in visibility. Write the prompt set first. Use buyer questions from sales calls, support tickets, customer research, and Search Console. Include research, comparison, and decision intent. Hold wording steady. Give each vendor the same prompts and record exact text, engine, location, date, and plan. Record limits. Capture included engines, prompt or credit limits, refresh cadence, add-ons, and trial restrictions. Ask how data was collected. Record API, browser, UI scraping, vendor-generated prompt, keyword-derived prompt, or panel source where stated. Repeat a sample yourself. Run five prompts in the same engines and compare the answer, mention, position, and citation with the platform record. Inspect citations. Confirm that the cited URL, domain, source category, or citation count means what the vendor says it means. Separate reporting from action. Note whether the vendor recommends, drafts, publishes, changes an AI-facing page, or leaves work to your team. Review the evidence. Keep reproducible or explainable results. Label one-off differences as directional. Frequently asked questions What is an LLM tracking tool? An LLM tracking tool is another name for an AI visibility platform. An LLM tracking tool samples answers from large language models and AI search interfaces and records brand mentions, citations, answer placement, sentiment, and competitors over time. The results are samples, so they show direction rather than a fixed rank. Do AI visibility platforms track conventional rankings? AI visibility platforms generally track brand presence inside generated answers, while conventional SEO platforms track pages in search results, clicks, impressions, and indexed-page signals. Some AI visibility platforms include technical audits or keyword context, but those fields do not turn an AI answer into a stable conventional ranking. Use both layers when the business depends on search traffic and answer inclusion. Conventional rankings show page performance in indexed search. AI visibility shows how systems describe, mention, or cite the brand during answer generation. Does one AI engine predict another? Visibility in one AI engine does not reliably predict visibility in another. Engines differ in retrieval, training data, web-search behavior, citation rules, updates, personalization, and interface. A strong result in ChatGPT does not establish the same result in Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Mode, or Google AI Overviews. Cross-engine tracking is useful when engine, prompt, location, date, and sampling method remain visible in the record. Do these platforms show real user queries? Most platforms do not provide complete access to live user query logs. They use controlled prompts, keyword-derived prompts, vendor-generated prompts, buyer-entered prompts, or modeled prompt volumes. Evertune states that EverPanel contains more than 150 million real user prompts. Profound's Prompt Volumes describes what people ask answer engines, and Ahrefs models prompts from its keyword database. Those sources add context, but they do not make every tracked answer a direct observation of a named user's session. Ask each vendor what “real” means in its product, and keep prompt origin separate from answer collection method. How often should teams sample AI visibility? Weekly sampling is a reasonable baseline for core prompts when the goal is directional trend detection. Daily sampling can fit a product launch, campaign, public issue, or fast experiment. Monthly sampling can fit lower-priority prompts with lower volatility. The right cadence depends on prompt volatility, competitive pressure, business impact, and run cost. Record the cadence with every comparison so a daily dataset is not compared casually with a monthly one. How can teams compare vendors fairly? Use the same prompts, engines, locations, date window, run cadence, competitor set, and evidence checks. Record what each plan includes rather than using the largest headline engine list. Compare raw response access, citation detail, trend retention, exports, governance, actionability, and price units. If a vendor does not disclose prompt origin, run count, retention, or a billing term, mark the field unavailable instead of guessing. Are AI visibility results exact rankings? AI visibility results are directional measurements, not fixed rankings. The same wording can produce different answers across runs, and prompt samples represent only the questions and contexts included. Use repeated measurements, manual spot checks, and analytics signals such as AI referral traffic or branded search to validate important trends. What should happen after a platform finds a gap? The next step depends on the platform and the gap. A report may identify a missing citation, inaccurate claim, competitor source, topic gap, or technical access issue. Some platforms rank recommendations. Others draft content, prepare outreach, publish through an approved CMS, or change an AI-facing version of a page. Review the evidence and approval path before treating a recommendation as a fix. Final decision Choose the platform that matches the measurement question and the work your team expects after measurement. Start with required engines and real buyer prompts. Then compare sampling, evidence, competitors, history, exports, governance, price units, and actionability. A controlled trial produces a more useful decision than a universal “best” list because it tests the prompts and workflows your business needs. text: You can rank first on Google and still be invisible the moment a buyer asks ChatGPT for a recommendation. AI visibility tools exist to measure that second surface: whether ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, Gemini, and Google AI Overviews name your brand when someone asks them a buying question. The market filled up fast. There are now dozens of platforms calling themselves AI visibility trackers, AI search monitors, or LLM visibility tools, and they range from a $29 prompt checker to enterprise suites with their own data pipelines. Most buyers cannot tell which one fits, or whether they need one at all. This guide answers that. It defines what these tools do, names the platforms B2B teams actually compare, lists the capabilities that separate a real tool from a vanity dashboard, and ends with the one decision a tool can never make for you. What are AI visibility tools? AI visibility tools are software that runs your buyer prompts through AI engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and Google AI Overviews, then reports whether each answer names your brand, links your site, or recommends a competitor instead. They turn "are we showing up in AI search" into a measurable number you can track week to week. Classic SEO tools cannot see this surface. Search Console (free) A no-cost first signal Google AI Overviews and AI Mode only First-party impressions, but no clicks or queries. Positioning reflects each vendor's public focus as of June 2026. Engine coverage and pricing change often, so confirm against a live trial before you commit. That distinction matters because the two jobs do not overlap. A rank tracker watches blue links. A visibility tool watches the synthesized answer above them. We mapped why those are now separate purchases in AI SEO tools: the two categories that matter . A dashboard tells you that you appeared. A visibility tool tells you whether you won. Why you need one: AI citations move every week The reason to instrument this surface is volatility. AI answers do not hold steady the way a Google ranking does. The sources a model cites this week are often gone the next, which means a one-time audit is stale before the invoice clears. The data is blunt. Scrunch analyzed 3.5 million citation events and found the median AI citation has a half-life of about 4.5 weeks : ChatGPT churns fastest at 3.4 weeks, Perplexity holds longest at 5.8. Separate research tracked by SISTRIX shows 40 to 60% of cited domains change month to month, and over six months most cited sources are completely different from where they started. Our own first-party AI search statistics , computed daily from more than 34,000 AI answers, show the same churn from the brand side: ChatGPT cites a source in 87% of answers, and the leading brand in a category flips in 24% of editions. The brand on top one week is not guaranteed the next. Visibility you measure once is visibility you have already lost. A content score is a grade you earn and keep. AI citation share is a moving target you have to re-read constantly, which is the entire argument for owning a tool rather than running a quarterly check. We unpack the mechanics in citation drift: why your AI visibility changes weekly . The 6 capabilities that separate a real tool from a dashboard Most platforms demo well. The gap shows up in what they measure once the trial ends. These are the six capabilities worth paying for. Anything missing more than one of them is a reporting widget, not a visibility tool. 1. It covers more than one AI engine If a tool only tracks ChatGPT, you are measuring one room in a house your buyers walk through entirely. Perplexity, Gemini, Google AI Overviews, and Copilot each pull from different source pools, and your brand can lead in one and vanish in another. Single-engine coverage gives you a confident number about a third of the picture. 2. It tracks at the prompt level, not the keyword level A real tool runs a named set of buyer prompts, the conversational questions your customers actually ask, not a list of keywords. Prompts are the new keywords, and the answer to "what is the best vendor for X" tells you more than your rank for "best X vendor" ever will. 3. It reports citation share of voice, not a yes or no flag "You appeared" is a vanity flag. The metric that survives a leadership meeting is share of voice: across your prompt set, how often an AI answer cites you versus the field. We defined the measurement in how to measure share of voice in AI search . 4. It shows who gets cited when you do not The most useful screen in any of these tools is the one that names the competitor cited in your place. That turns a missing citation into a target. Knowing you are absent is half the job; knowing who took the slot tells you which source pool to break into. 5. It connects a missing citation to a fixable page A number on a dashboard is not an action. The stronger tools link an absent citation to the specific page that should have earned it, so the output is a rebuild queue. A tool that only reports the gap leaves the hardest work, deciding what to change, on your desk. 6. It alerts you when your share drifts Given the weekly churn, a monthly export is too slow. The capability that matters is a drift alert: a signal when your citation share drops on a prompt that was working. That is the difference between catching a slide in days and discovering it a quarter later. Your competitors are not the benchmark. The model's source pool is. Here is how the main ones position themselves, so you can match the tool to your situation rather than the loudest demo. We cover the full set in GEO tools: the complete landscape for 2026 . Profound is built for enterprise and regulated industries Profound targets larger and compliance-bound teams, carrying SOC 2 and HIPAA coverage that healthcare, finance, and legal buyers need before they can adopt anything. The analytics run deep, and the price matches the audience. Peec AI is the mid-market analytics specialist Peec AI is a pure-play AI search analytics platform that raised $29M and reached more than $4M in ARR inside ten months. Its standout for global B2B teams is unlimited countries and languages at every tier, which matters if your buyers research in more than one market. Scrunch organizes around monitor, analyze, and optimize Scrunch frames its platform as three jobs rather than one dashboard: monitor where you are cited, analyze why, and optimize the pages that should earn more. It tracks ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, and Copilot, with persona and funnel modeling on higher tiers. Otterly is the cheapest way to get a baseline Otterly is the most accessible tool on the list, with an entry plan around $29 a month that tracks a small set of prompts across ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, and Copilot. It is a fine first baseline, not a long-term operations hub. AthenaHQ is built for PR and brand teams AthenaHQ leans into narrative: how AI describes your brand, and when prospects research your category but a competitor gets cited. That competitor-displacement view makes it a favorite with communications teams rather than technical SEO teams. The free option is Google Search Console On June 3, 2026, Google added generative AI performance reports to Search Console , giving site owners their first first-party view of how often their pages appear in AI Overviews and AI Mode. It is free and credible, with one large catch covered below. A vanity dashboard shows you: • A single "you were mentioned" flag • One engine, usually ChatGPT • A monthly export you read once A real visibility tool shows you: • Citation share across every major engine • The exact prompts where a competitor wins instead • The specific page to rebuild, and an alert when share drops What AI visibility tools cannot do Before you treat any subscription as the answer, know the limits. They are real, and the honest vendors say so. No tool can see inside Google's ranking Google now names AEO and GEO directly and published guidance on third-party SEO tools stating plainly that third-party tools do not have access to its internal ranking data and cannot guarantee performance. Any vendor promising a guaranteed lift in AI citations is overstating what they can measure. No tool can promise an AI citation. Anyone who does is selling you a number Google says they cannot see. The free Search Console report is impressions only Google's new AI report is a genuine first-party signal, but it ships impressions, pages, countries, and devices and explicitly no clicks, no click-through rate, and no query data. It tells you that you appeared, not whether anyone acted, and it only covers Google's own surfaces. You still need multi-engine coverage for ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Claude. A tool surfaces the gap; a person closes it Every platform here ends at the same place: a screen showing what is wrong. None of them write the answer block, fix the entity description, or earn the third-party proof that wins the citation back. If no one owns that weekly rebuild decision, a managed AI visibility service runs the measurement and the fix loop so the data turns into recovered citations instead of a prettier chart. How to choose your AI visibility tool Work through this in order. You do not need every tool, you need the one that fits where your buyers research. • Run a free baseline first. Google Search Console plus a trial of one tracker tells you whether you have a problem before you commit budget. • Confirm the tool covers the engines your buyers use, not just ChatGPT. Check Perplexity, Gemini, and AI Overviews coverage explicitly. • Insist on citation share of voice, not a mention flag. A "you appeared" number cannot be defended in a leadership review. • Match the tier to your markets. If you sell in more than one language, multi-country coverage is a requirement, not an upgrade. • Decide who owns the weekly rebuild before you buy. The tool is the cheap part. The person who acts on it is the program. The full audit method, including how to build the prompt set, lives in how to run an AI visibility audit . For the team side of the decision, our managed GEO program pairs the tracking with the people who close the gaps. FAQ What are the best AI visibility tools? There is no single best, because they serve different teams. Profound fits enterprise and regulated buyers, Peec AI fits mid-market analytics teams that need many languages, Scrunch fits teams that want to act on the data, Otterly fits the smallest budgets, and AthenaHQ fits PR and brand teams. Most B2B teams start with a free Search Console baseline plus one paid tracker. What is an AI visibility platform? An AI visibility platform is software that runs your buyer prompts across multiple AI engines and reports how often each one cites or recommends your brand. The stronger platforms add competitor tracking, share-of-voice scoring, and a queue of pages to rebuild, rather than a single "you appeared" flag. How much do AI visibility tools cost? Entry tools start around $29 a month for a small set of prompts on one or two engines. Mid-market analytics platforms run into the hundreds per month, and enterprise suites with compliance coverage and many languages are priced on request. Google Search Console's AI report is free but covers only Google's surfaces and shows impressions, not clicks. Do I need an AI visibility tool or a free tracker? A free tracker and Search Console are enough to learn whether you have a problem. You need a paid tool once you are tracking a real prompt set across several engines every week, because the citation churn of 40 to 60% a month makes one-time checks useless. Sustained measurement needs either a paid plan or a managed service. What is LLM visibility tracking? LLM visibility tracking is the same job described by a different name: measuring whether large language models like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini cite or recommend your brand in their answers. The tools listed here all do it; the label varies because the category is still settling on its vocabulary. The tool tracks whether ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and AI Overviews cite your brand, and the good ones turn that into a share-of-voice number, a competitor view, and a rebuild queue. But the tool is the cheap, easy half. It tells you where you are losing. It does not fix the page, and Google has said plainly that no third party can guarantee the citation comes back. Run a free baseline, pick one tracker that covers more than ChatGPT, and put a person in charge of the weekly decision. So a daily figure should be read as an average, not as news. ScryRank checks once a month : the second criterion where it loses, if you need to see the effect of a change within a week. How to build the question set is in prompt tracking . We have several locations: can we measure each one? Only with some tools, and rarely below country level on the base plan. Otterly fixes one country per prompt, SE Visible one location per project, and Semrush states 68,000+ locations only in its Brand Performance report. With five branches, the maths goes: prompts per branch, times engines, times locations. On Ahrefs, where one check is one prompt on one engine in one location, 50 prompts on 3 engines in 5 cities already make 750 checks per update . Businesses with several branches are covered in local AI visibility . Which AI visibility tools support multi-client dashboards? Peec, Otterly, Rankscale and Profound have agency plans or features; Semrush keeps multi-brand for Enterprise and SE Visible has no white label. For an agency three things count: cost per client, separate permissions and a report you can send under your own brand. Peec gives each client an isolated project, plus pitch projects for proposals. Otterly's Agency Partner status adds Looker Studio reports with the agency's branding. What goes into the monthly report is in the AI visibility report . Which AI search visibility tools integrate with Looker, Google Analytics or existing marketing dashboards? Looker Studio connects to Otterly (from Standard), Peec (from Advanced), Ahrefs (from Advanced) and Rankscale (from Pro). None of the 8 states a native GA4 integration on its entry plan: Otterly offers a Looker template for GA4, and Profound lists Google Analytics on Enterprise only. Do you really need it? Yes, if the figure has to sit next to sales. Visibility in answers and the traffic it sends are two different measures: you isolate the second in GA4, as we show in ChatGPT traffic in Google Analytics . Trial and price: how to compare them without falling for "from" Compare price per prompt and per engine, not per plan. Otterly Lite costs $29 for 15 prompts, almost $2 a prompt; SE Visible Basic $99 for 200 prompts, under 50 cents, but billed annually. Extra engines cost money: on Otterly Standard, AI Mode and Gemini are $59 a month each , Claude $109. On Ahrefs, Claude uses 8 checks per update instead of one. Semrush and Ahrefs offer no trial of the AI module. The full bill, with free tools and third-party trials, is in AI visibility tool pricing . Official pages contradict each other (and what to ask the vendor before signing) Of the 8 tools, 2 have official pages that say different things on the same point. Another 3 (Peec, Ahrefs and our own ScryRank) don't state at least one of the criteria in the comparison: trial length, multi-client management or integrations. The two contradictions we found on 27 October 2026: Otterly : the homepage says "7-day free trial" in the FAQ and "Free 14-Day Trial" in the sign-up panel; the pricing page shows two price lists, with Lite at $29 and at $25, without saying which applies to monthly billing. Semrush : the toolkit knowledge base page says the AI module has no trial; the Italian getting-started guide ends with "try Semrush free for seven days", which applies to the suite, not the module. Then there's SE Visible , whose homepage lists 7 tracked countries. The UK is there. Italy, where we did this check, isn't. So does it matter if your market is covered? It's the whole point. Before signing, ask in writing for four things: whether your country is a tracking location (not just the interface language), which engines are included in the plan you're buying, what happens to prompts when credits run out, and whether the history stays yours when you cancel. A year's subscription on the wrong engine. It's the most expensive mistake we see: a tool picked on price that doesn't read AI Mode or doesn't track your country, and twelve months of reports that decide nothing. We start from your customers' real questions and tell you which engines, which locations and how many questions need measuring, before you choose the tool. Book a strategy call How to test a tool in a 7-day trial (the protocol we use) A trial is for checking that the tool's figures match what you see with your own eyes, not for exploring the dashboard. Seven days are enough if you arrive with the questions already written. Day 1: load 20 real questions , written the way a customer would, none with your brand name. Add 2 or 3 competitors and your country. Day 2: ask 5 of those questions by hand on ChatGPT and on Google, and save the answers. They're your benchmark. Days 3-5: open 10 full answers in the tool . Check the highlighted brand is really there and the cited sources are real links. Day 6: see how the same question changes from one day to the next. If the tool only shows the latest answer, you don't have a history. Day 7: export to CSV or Looker Studio, and work out the cost per prompt and per engine on the plan you'd buy. Twenty questions show whether the tool works. Reading a market takes more : on client projects we start from at least 50 questions per service. How much answer variability weighs on a tool's figures is what we measure in how accurate AI visibility data is . And if there's no trial, as with Semrush or Ahrefs? Run the same protocol in the first paid month and choose monthly billing. The annual discount isn't worth a year of data you can't use. What makes you citable, and what no tool tells you An AI visibility tool measures whether and how you appear in AI Overviews, AI Mode and ChatGPT answers; it doesn't make you appear. What raises the odds of being cited is knowing which pages the AI reads on your sector's questions and working on those: your own pages, industry portals, reviews. That's why, among the ten criteria, the cited-sources view is worth more than the score. In our test of the tools the AIs recommend , Perplexity used a Visilay guide as a source but didn't name ScryRank in its answer: being read and being named are two different metrics, and a good tool keeps them apart. Work on sources is what we do in our GEO service . Two things none of the 8 tools can see. First: the answer your customer actually saw . AI answers change with account, history and location; tools query the engines with neutral, fixed settings, and the figure works as a trend across many questions. Second: Google's and Microsoft's own data on your site . Since June 2026 Search Console has generative AI performance reports , and since February 2026 Bing Webmaster Tools shows in AI Performance how often your pages are cited in Copilot and Bing's AI summaries. Both cost nothing and should be opened before you buy anything. How to read them alongside external tools is in our AI visibility guide . If you'd rather not choose and configure anything, our AI Monitoring service does it for you: questions, engines, competitors and a monthly read of the data. Frequently asked questions What is the most important criterion when choosing an AI visibility tool? It depends: for most businesses it's coverage of your customers' engines on the plan you buy, meaning ChatGPT, Gemini, AI Overviews and AI Mode. Next comes keeping brand mentions separate from cited sources, because that's what tells you where to act. Can an AI visibility tool guarantee ChatGPT will cite my brand? No. A tool measures whether and how you appear in answers; it doesn't change them. Anyone promising guaranteed citations is selling something else: the odds of being cited grow by working on the sources the AI reads in your sector. Can I check AI visibility by hand without a tool? Yes, to start with: 20 questions asked by hand on ChatGPT and Google give you a first snapshot. It doesn't hold up over time, though, because answers change on their own and without history you can't tell a random swing from a trend. Should I use the AI module of my SEO suite or a dedicated tool? It depends: if you already pay for Semrush or Ahrefs, their module saves you a second suite, but Semrush includes 1 project and 25 prompts with no trial. Dedicated tools such as Peec or Otterly give more control over sources, engines and exports. How long should a test last before choosing? It depends on the tool: 7 days are enough if you arrive with 20 questions already written and compare 5 answers with what you see by hand. If there's no trial, use the first month on monthly billing. Do AI visibility tools work for the UK market? Yes, but the interface language isn't enough: check that your country is a tracking location on the plan you buy. On 27 October 2026 SE Visible's homepage listed the UK among 7 tracked countries, and Semrush stated 220+ countries for prompt tracking. In short Your customers' engines first, price second. AI Mode and AI Overviews are two surfaces: check the plan covers both. Cited sources are worth more than the score. Cost per prompt and per engine, not per plan. Seven trial days with 20 real questions. One last thing the check taught us. These tools measure answers that change every day, and their own pages change faster than vendors can keep them aligned: for 5 tools out of 8 we found a contradiction or a missing detail on at least one criterion. The criterion that sums up the rest is simple: choose the tool that shows you where each of its numbers comes from . The one that doesn't will, sooner or later, ask you to take it on trust. text: AI Visibility Platform Comparison: 17 Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) Tools for 2027 Last updated: October 26, 2026 AI visibility and Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) tools help businesses measure, analyze, and improve how their brands appear in AI-generated answers from ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Perplexity, Claude, and other AI platforms. These tools track brand mentions, citations, sentiment, competitive share of voice, and recommendations. More advanced platforms connect that intelligence to content optimization, technical improvements, and marketing workflows. This guide compares 17 AI visibility and GEO tools for 2027, explains their distinguishing capabilities, and provides a practical framework for selecting the right platform based on business objectives, organizational needs, and the ability to turn visibility data into measurable improvements. Schedule a Brandi AI Demo » Key Takeaways AI visibility requires different measurements from traditional SEO. Search rankings, clicks, and organic traffic do not fully reveal how AI platforms mention, cite, recommend, or characterize a brand. AI visibility monitoring and GEO optimization serve different purposes. Monitoring identifies where a brand appears in AI answers. GEO intelligence and optimization help teams understand visibility gaps and prioritize improvements. The best GEO tools provide more than dashboards. Competitive benchmarking, citation analysis, brand sentiment, prompt-level tracking, and actionable recommendations help organizations translate data into marketing decisions. Platform capabilities vary significantly. Some tools emphasize affordable monitoring, while others focus on enterprise intelligence, brand perception, content creation, technical optimization, or integration with existing SEO platforms. There is no universally best AI visibility platform. The right choice depends on which AI engines customers use, the depth of intelligence required, available resources, and how effectively a team can act on the findings. Effective GEO is an ongoing discipline. Brands need consistent measurement, credible content, technical accessibility, and continuous evaluation as AI systems and buyer behavior evolve. Table of Contents Why AI Visibility Tools Matter in 2027 The way consumers and business buyers discover, research, and evaluate brands is changing. Instead of relying exclusively on traditional search results, buyers increasingly ask AI platforms to recommend products, compare vendors, evaluate capabilities, and explain purchasing considerations. Research illustrates the growing importance of this behavior. According to G2 , 51% of B2B software buyers surveyed in March 2026 reported starting their research with an AI chatbot more often than Google, compared with 29% in April 2025. Separately, Forrester’s research on generative AI adoption among B2B buyers highlights the technology’s expanding role in purchasing decisions. For businesses, this creates a visibility challenge that traditional marketing analytics cannot fully address. A company may rank highly in Google search results yet remain absent when a prospective customer asks ChatGPT to recommend solutions in its category. Another brand might appear frequently but be described using outdated information, unfavorable comparisons, or messaging that does not reflect its current capabilities. These differences matter because AI-generated answers can influence customer perceptions before buyers visit a website or engage with a sales representative. AI visibility tools help organizations understand that emerging layer of discovery. Rather than simply counting website visits or search impressions, they examine what AI systems communicate about brands and the information sources that appear alongside those responses. The strategic question is no longer just whether customers can find a company’s website. It is whether AI systems accurately represent that company when buyers seek information, comparisons, and recommendations. What Are AI Visibility and Generative Engine Optimization Tools? AI visibility tools are software platforms that track and analyze how brands, products, and organizations appear in AI-generated answers. Depending on their capabilities, these platforms measure brand mentions, citations, sentiment, competitive presence, recommendation frequency, and visibility across different AI engines. Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) tools build on those measurements to identify opportunities for improving a brand’s representation in AI-generated content. GEO platforms may analyze the sources cited by AI, identify competitive content gaps, recommend website improvements, and help marketing teams develop content that addresses questions buyers ask AI systems. The terms AI visibility, GEO, and Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) frequently overlap, but they emphasize different aspects of AI-driven discovery. Discipline Primary focus Typical measurements or activities Search Engine Optimization (SEO) Improving visibility in traditional and AI-enhanced search experiences Rankings, impressions, organic traffic, crawlability, and conversions Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) Making information clear and accessible for direct answers Answer-oriented content, factual clarity, structured information, and extractability Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) Improving brand inclusion and representation in generative AI responses Mentions, citations, recommendations, competitive visibility, and content improvements AI Visibility Monitoring Measuring how AI platforms currently represent a brand Prompt tracking, citation frequency, sentiment, and competitive share of voice These disciplines are complementary. SEO helps establish the technical accessibility, content relevance, and authority that also support AI discovery. AEO emphasizes information that can be understood and used in answers. GEO extends these efforts to how brands are represented across generative systems. For example, a cybersecurity provider may rank well for enterprise security software but be omitted when a buyer asks an AI assistant to compare solutions for regulated financial institutions. An effective GEO program would investigate which competitors appear, what information the AI cites, and whether the provider’s content adequately addresses regulatory requirements and buyer concerns. AI Visibility Monitoring vs. GEO Intelligence: What’s the Difference? One of the most important distinctions when evaluating GEO software is the difference between monitoring AI visibility and generating actionable intelligence. AI visibility monitoring answers questions such as whether a brand appears in ChatGPT recommendations, how frequently it is mentioned across a defined prompt set, and which competitors appear alongside it. These measurements establish a useful baseline, but they do not necessarily explain what marketers should do next. AI visibility intelligence adds several layers of analysis. It examines how AI characterizes a brand, which sources are cited, where competitors dominate important buying-intent questions, and which information gaps may contribute to weaker visibility. For example, a monitoring dashboard might report that a cybersecurity provider appears in 20% of relevant AI responses while a competing provider appears in 60%. A more advanced platform could help identify whether the competitor has stronger coverage of regulatory requirements, more detailed product comparisons, or frequently cited third-party research. Those findings provide a basis for deciding whether to improve product pages, publish original research, expand technical documentation, or pursue relevant earned media. The distinction is important because measurement identifies the visibility gap, while intelligence helps organizations decide how to address it. Neither can guarantee that a future AI response will include a particular brand. What Features Should You Look for in an AI Visibility Platform? Before comparing vendors, organizations should establish consistent evaluation criteria. Feature lists alone can be misleading because platforms differ in how they collect AI responses, calculate scores, identify sources, and translate insights into recommendations. 1. Multi-Engine AI Visibility Tracking A strong platform should monitor the AI systems that prospective customers actually use. Depending on the target audience, these may include ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, Perplexity, Claude, Microsoft Copilot, Meta AI, and Grok. Coverage should be evaluated at the subscription-plan level rather than relying on a vendor’s overall list of supported platforms. Organizations should also confirm whether monitoring uses live responses, APIs, sampled queries, or another collection method. 2. Prompt-Level Tracking and Buyer Intent AI visibility is highly dependent on the questions buyers ask. A platform should support representative prompts covering category discovery, product comparisons, purchase considerations, alternatives, technical requirements, and buyer pain points. Organizations should also consider whether the software helps identify relevant prompts rather than requiring marketers to develop every query manually. 3. Competitive Share of Voice GEO Share of Voice measures a brand’s relative presence against competitors across a defined set of AI-generated responses. Unlike traditional search share of voice, GEO analysis focuses on inclusion in generated answers and recommendations rather than search-result rankings alone. Because platforms calculate these metrics differently, organizations should examine the underlying methodology before comparing results. 4. Citation and Source Analysis Citation analysis identifies the websites, publications, and other sources that AI systems reference when producing answers. This information helps marketing and communications teams discover which external sources frequently appear in relevant discussions and whether their own content is being cited. A platform should distinguish between a brand mention, a citation to the brand’s website, and a reference to an external source discussing that brand. 5. Brand Sentiment and Narrative Framing Appearing in an AI response is not necessarily positive. An AI system might recommend a company, describe it neutrally, associate it with limitations, or repeat outdated information. Sentiment and framing analysis help organizations understand how their brand is characterized, which attributes are emphasized, and whether competitors are presented more favorably. 6. Actionable GEO Recommendations Some platforms primarily display monitoring data. Others recommend specific improvements to website content, FAQs, technical documentation, thought leadership, and other assets. Organizations should prioritize tools that connect recommendations to identifiable visibility gaps, supporting evidence, and realistic marketing actions. 7. Geographic and Multilingual Coverage Global organizations should evaluate whether platforms support country-specific, regional, and multilingual monitoring. AI-generated responses can vary by language, market, and location, making geographic coverage especially important for international brands and agencies. 8. Reporting, Integrations, and Organizational Fit A platform should match the way the organization manages marketing and communications activities. Relevant considerations include dashboards, exports, API availability, analytics integrations, reporting permissions, agency workspaces, security requirements, and collaboration capabilities. The most sophisticated software is not necessarily the best investment if the organization cannot consistently use its insights.
